subject: Clarification on Pricing Exhibit — caps, floors and packaging credits
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@genesishealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing exhibit v3 — ambiguous floor/cap language

Connor / Laura,

Thanks again for the meeting earlier. Attached is the latest Pricing Exhibit (v3) that our procurement/legal team received from your side. We have two areas where we need fast clarification before we can move to redlines:

1) Floor trigger and grace period: Section 2(b) appears to allow a one-quarter true-up but doesn't say whether credits generated during the grace period are netted or held in escrow. That affects our internal budgeting.

2) Packaging credits and bundle conversion: The exhibit references a "packaging conversion mechanism" but the math in Exhibit A (fee table) doesn't match the example in the Order Form notes. If the conversion applies retroactively, that materially changes our commit.

We'd appreciate a short written interpretation that we can share with procurement. We're aiming to finalize the exhibit by Friday, 8/07.

Attached: Genesis_Pricing_Exhibit_v3.pdf

Best,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Dir. Vendor Contracts, Genesis Health

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@genesishealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit v3 — ambiguous floor/cap language

Elena — thanks for the note and the PDF. I've read through the two points and pulled together our initial read and proposed clarifying edits (attached as "exhibit_v3_annotated.pdf"). High-level:

- Floor trigger/grace period: The intent on our side is to net credits against the next billing cycle rather than hold in escrow. Practically that means a customer won't see a separate "escrow" line item; the true-up will reduce the following invoice.
  - Proposed edit: change Section 2(b) last sentence to: "Credits arising during a grace period will be applied against the next billing cycle within 30 days unless otherwise expressly agreed."

- Packaging conversion: The example in Exhibit A was illustrative and not intended to be retroactive. If Genesis requires retroactive application we can draft a specific true-up mechanism, but default behavior is prospective only.
  - Proposed edit: add a short definition to Exhibit A: "Packaging Conversion (prospective): adjustments apply to months following conversion only; no retroactive token reallocation."

I've attached a quick comparison spreadsheet (pricing-comparison-redline.xlsx) that maps the example math to the table values — that should make the mismatch easier to follow. Karthik, Laura: can you weigh in on the legal/ops acceptability of the language above?

Next steps: if Genesis is OK with netting credits and prospective conversion, we can produce a clean exhibit for signature and send the DocuSign link. If they require escrow/retroactivity we'll need to scope operational impacts and present a small amendment fee.

Thanks — available for a 20-min call this afternoon if that helps.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0123

Attachments: exhibit_v3_annotated.pdf; pricing-comparison-redline.xlsx

Elena, Connor — quick note from the commercial side.

Appreciate the flag on the prospective vs retroactive behavior. From a sales perspective, we'd prefer the netting approach Connor outlined — it keeps implementation simple for both teams and avoids surprise credits spanning multiple invoices. If Genesis is risk-averse on that point, we can offer a one-time transition credit (capped) to bridge any perceived gap, rather than opening an ongoing escrow mechanism.

Suggested concession (if required): 1 month of packaging-credit protection up to $25k (one-time). This would be conditional on signing within 7 days of final exhibit. Let us know if that moves the needle.

Connor — please confirm operations/finance implications for the transition credit and, Laura, please confirm legal is comfortable documenting the netting language + conditional concession.

Thanks,
Karthik

Thanks all — I reviewed Connor's proposed edits and Karthik's concession. Below are legal's recommended replacements and a short list of action items. I've attached a clean markup (exhibit_v3_annotated.pdf) and a tracked-change .xlsx for commercial review.

Legal suggestions (high level):
1) Replace Connor's proposed sentence in Section 2(b) with the following to remove ambiguity around timing and offsetting: "Credits generated during a grace period shall be applied as an offset to the immediately subsequent invoice(s) within the next billing cycle; if not applied within 60 days, such credits shall be refunded to the Customer upon request."
   - Rationale: gives Genesis a remedy if internal processes would otherwise delay offsetting; preserves our netting preference but provides a limited fallback.

2) Packaging Conversion — be explicit about non-retroactivity and include a worked example in Exhibit A. I recommend adding: "For clarity, Packaging Conversion adjustments are prospective only. For example, if Customer converts 3 packs to single-sku on June 15, adjustments will apply to invoices dated July 1 onward. No retrospective invoice reallocation prior to July 1 will be made."

3) Concession language: If we accept Karthik's one-time credit, capture the cap and the sign-by window and specify offset mechanics so accounting can implement it without manual exceptions.

Action items:
- Connor: confirm with Ops/Finance whether the 60-day fallback is operationally feasible and whether an automated invoice offset can be implemented (or whether a manual refund workflow is required).
- Karthik: confirm commercial approval of the $25k cap and the sign-by date.
- Elena/Genesis: if acceptable, confirm and we will prepare a final clean exhibit and DocuSign envelope.

Attachments: exhibit_v3_annotated.pdf; pricing-comparison-redline.xlsx
